messages.author: Timothy Giese
messages.body:
"WARNING: buffer overflow detected" occurs in the function XmuSnprintf defined within AmberTools/src/leap/sac/Xmu/Lower.c
It looks like it is a function that writes formatted data from a variable argument list to a fixed size buffer, but the number of characters to be written exceeds the allocated size of the string buffer.  Hard to say what is triggering this, but I wonder if there's long strings of text in receptor.mol2 or the leap input? Just throwing ideas at the wall here: was receptor.mol2 created or edited on a windows machine and the line return characters aren't being handled correctly?

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Mon, Dec 16, 2024, Timothy Giese via AMBER wrote:
>"WARNING: buffer overflow detected" occurs in the function XmuSnprintf
>defined within AmberTools/src/leap/sac/Xmu/Lower.c
I don't think the above is correct, since the line Tim quotes is not
actually compiled, and tleap should not be using the Xmu code.
But that is not important: as Tim has said, what we need is to see the
receptor.mol2 file, since loading that file is the step where this
warning/error occurs.  The code that implements loadMol2 is pretty
straightforward, and it should(!) be fairly straightforward to figure out
exactly what is going on, as long as we have an input mol2 file that
triggers the problem.
...thx....dac
